In detail

The XX Settembre area, around Via XX Settembre and Castro Pretorio, is a largely institutional and residential district of ministries, the Ministero della Difesa, and the US Embassy annex, bordering Termini station to its south. It sits at the edge of the official Termini/Esquilino "zona rossa" enhanced-surveillance zone and has seen some spillover of the same predatory-crime and drug-dealing concerns documented there. The government/embassy character of the area keeps a visible security presence, and no pattern of serious or recurring violent crime specific to this zone was found beyond that.

Frequently asked questions

Is XX Settembre safe?

Wandroz currently rates XX Settembre in Rome as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rome during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Is XX Settembre safe at night?

At night, XX Settembre is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

XX Settembre's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rome) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
